messages:
zoe: heads-up: after the nightly batch on gnode-77 we saw sustained iowait and two pods failed with EIO. attaching quick logs.

zoe: iostat -x 1 3

Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1          0.00  0.00 120.00 800.00 9600   64000    80      12.3    45.6   10.2    48.0   0.30  98.5

zoe: smartctl shows reallocated sectors and media errors:

SMART Attributes Data:
(177) Program_Fail_Count    1
(179) Wear_Leveling_Count  40
Error Count: 15

samir: thanks, any kernel oops or io errors in dmesg?

zoe: dmesg has nvme error log: "nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, aborting"

lina: @infra-bot can you list affected nodes and pods?

infra-bot: ALERT: ephemeral-disk-failure detected on 3 nodes: gnode-77, gnode-82, gnode-83. Pods failing: nightly-batch-*/job-runner. AlertID: A-2026-9842. Link: https://redwood.ai/ops/alerts/A-2026-9842

samir: are these on the same AZ / hardware batch? might be firmware regression from 2024-11 nvme fw.

zoe: yes all are in us-west-2a, same host type p4d-local, provisioned 2024-10.

lina: our ephemeral-cleaner daemonset logs show "removing mountpoint failed: target busy" and cleanup pods crashloop on these nodes. that leaves stale mounts preventing fsck.

zoe: paste from cleaner log:

time="2026-02-28T03:12:11Z" level=error msg="failed to unmount /var/lib/kubelet/pods/abcde-12345/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir: target busy"

ops-oncall: propose immediate action: cordon + drain gnode-77/82/83, stop scheduling, run full fsck offline, then fstrim + firmware check. Also throttle batch windows.

samir: agree. we should also reduce concurrency on nightly-batch from 40 -> 12 while we triage.

lina: note: kubelet eviction thresholds are default, but spikes in iops cause kubelet/oomkiller to evict cleanup pods. we should set evictionHard for ephemeral-storage at 90% and restart the daemonset with more privileged mounts to properly unmount.

zoe: cost question: replacing 3 NVMe nodes vs migrating these jobs to io2 (network) for the short term. rough numbers: 3 x local NVMe host replacement ~ $18k + downtime. Moving to io2 for nightly batch (additional 10TB) ~ $2.5k/month. thoughts?

samir: temporary io2 is cheaper short-term; long-term if hardware failing batch maybe RMA and replace. we should document SLA for ephemeral disks to avoid hidden costs.

ops-oncall: I'll open ticket and schedule rolling reprovision for affected host batch. ticket: INF-1972. ETA first review 2h.

lina: also file a bug for the cleaner: it needs to fallback to lazy unmount (umount -l) and retry, with a kubelet pre-stop hook to ensure mounts are released. add exponential backoff.

zoe: for triage, I'm running fsck -y on gnode-77 now (unmounted). will attach results to INF-1972. Also running smartctl -a for full batch and comparing vendor firmware.

ops-oncall: done, cordoned gnode-77/82/83. INF-1972 created and linked: https://redwood.ai/infra/INF-1972. Scheduling RMA planning meeting in 48h.

infra-bot: follow-up alert will post when node rejoin happens or if additional nodes trip similar errors.

zoe: thanks team, will update when fsck finishes (running now). :thumbsup:
